resources.name: Blender
resources.category: A7. Native applications and procedural tools
resources.role: Headless 3D rendering, Python scene build and compositing from the macOS app bundle
resources.summary: Full 3D authoring suite driven in background mode: a .blend file or a Python-built scene renders one frame or a range to PNG or EXR with alpha, under Workbench for speed, EEVEE for real-time quality or Cycles for path tracing. The compositor and simulation caches cover what VCR's own layers cannot yet. Blender keeps its own clock, so frame N is frame N.
use_when: Path-traced product shots, cloth, fluids, particles with baked caches
An existing .blend from a designer must render in a production
Render passes and compositor work before VCR's compositor lands
Over Three.js when minutes per frame are acceptable for the look
avoid_when: Fast iteration on a web-native look: Three.js in seconds
Simple 2D or typography: SVG, GSAP or p5.js
You need a scriptable 2D animation app: Synfig or Manim

facets.one_line: Frame and range renders from the CLI, option ordering, output paths
Factory-settings scenes built in bpy, enums read not guessed, seeds recorded
Node tree by type, render passes to multilayer EXR
Workbench, EEVEE and Cycles: speed, quality and what is byte-stable

notes: Not on PATH on macOS; use the app bundle executable. First native application spike planned in M0.

evidence.result: Workbench background render of one 320x240 RGBA frame from the app bundle

resources.name: FFmpeg / ffprobe
resources.role: Native encoding, muxing, filtergraphs, probing and sequence assembly; every renderer's delivery path
resources.summary: The command-line media toolchain. Every renderer's output becomes video here: image sequences to H.264, VP9 or ProRes 4444 with alpha, audio muxing, overlays and crossfades in filtergraphs, trims and concatenation, and ffprobe as the inspection tool the examples diff against. Deterministic in metadata and frames per build, not in container bytes.
use_when: Any encode, mux, trim, concatenate or probe
Assembling an image sequence from any renderer into a deliverable
Overlaying flat layers with alpha before VCR's compositor exists
Verifying a render: frame count, fps, duration, pixel format
avoid_when: Editorial decisions: those belong in VCR's timeline, FFmpeg gets resolved intervals
In-browser conversion with no native binary: Mediabunny or ffmpeg.wasm
Shot detection or scene splitting: PySceneDetect drives FFmpeg for you
GIF quality matters: encode frames with gifski

facets.one_line: Codecs and pixel formats for web, alpha and intermediate delivery
Combine audio and video, concatenate, who is authoritative on duration
Overlay with alpha, crossfade, scale and colour range
ffprobe JSON as evidence and as a test oracle
Sequence clocks, holds, gaps and rounding

resources.license: LGPL-2.1 or GPL depending on build flags

resources.name: GSAP
resources.role: Paused, seekable timelines for DOM and SVG motion; the clock for every browser scene
resources.summary: Animation library that writes CSS transforms and SVG attributes from a timeline you build once and seek from outside. In VCR every browser scene exposes one paused GSAP timeline; the capture harness seeks it frame by frame, so output is a pure function of time. Plugins cover motion along SVG paths, per-character text, stroke reveals and shape morphs.
use_when: Any DOM or SVG motion that must be seeked from outside: title cards, lower thirds, kinetic type
Over Anime.js when you need labels, nested timelines and the plugin set
Over CSS animations whenever frames must be captured deterministically
Orchestrating several elements against one clock with relative positions
avoid_when: Canvas or WebGL content: drive p5.js or Three.js from t directly instead
Spring physics is the point: Motion or React Spring sample springs natively
You need a visual curve editor: Theatre.js, then export values

facets.one_line: Build, nest, label and seek one paused timeline per scene
Named and custom easing curves and when each reads well
Move and auto-rotate elements along an SVG path
Per-character and per-line text animation, font-load safe

resources.license: GSAP standard licence (free including plugins since 3.13; recheck)

evidence.result: 90 frames seeked and captured with alpha; shuffled order matches sequential; see specifications/spikes/browser-capture.md

resources.name: p5.js
resources.role: Generative 2D and WebGL sketches written as a pure function of time and seed
resources.summary: Creative-coding library with the broadest beginner-to-expert API for procedural 2D, simple WebGL, noise and randomness. In VCR a sketch runs with noLoop and redraws for the time the harness asks for, resetting its seeds every frame, so particle fields, flow fields and noise textures capture deterministically.
use_when: Procedural backgrounds, particles, flow fields and noise-driven abstracts
Over Pts or canvas-sketch when you want the largest API and example base
Quick 2D experiments where a scene graph would be overhead
Data-driven abstract visuals from a small JSON input
avoid_when: Real 3D with lights, materials and loaders: Three.js
Vector output that a designer must edit afterwards: SVG with GSAP
Sprite-heavy scenes with thousands of objects: PixiJS
Typography layout: SVG or Satori

facets.one_line: noLoop, redraw from t, reset noiseSeed and randomSeed per frame
Transparent clear, transforms, colour modes
Centred origin, per-frame lights, loaded fonts
Seeded Perlin noise as the deterministic motion source

resources.name: SVG
resources.role: Dependency-free vector source for cards, logos and diagrams; rasterised by resvg or a browser
resources.summary: The vector format every tool here reads and writes. Static SVG rasterises deterministically with resvg; animated SVG runs inline in a browser scene driven by GSAP. Designers can edit the source, Graphviz and Mermaid emit it, and SVGO shrinks it. Keep colour and layout in the SVG and motion in the timeline.
use_when: Title cards, lower thirds, logos and diagrams that must stay editable and scale to any size
Stroke-draw reveals and shape morphs over a transparent background
Output from Graphviz, Mermaid, D3 or Inkscape entering a production
A fixture that needs no dependencies at all
avoid_when: Photographic or heavily filtered content at 4K: filters are slow in browsers
Hundreds of animated elements: PixiJS or p5.js canvas
SMIL animation: it cannot be seeked from outside and resvg ignores it

facets.one_line: viewBox, stable ids, fonts to paths, colour separate from motion
Why SMIL is out and GSAP plugins are in
resvg for stills, the capture harness for motion, one AA convention per production

notes: Core alongside GSAP: static SVG is a native, dependency-free source format; GSAP supplies the timeline.

resources.name: Three.js
resources.role: Browser 3D rendered once per seek with alpha: product shots, hero objects, camera moves
resources.summary: The standard WebGL and WebGPU scene graph for the browser, with loaders, PBR materials, lights, shadows, postprocessing and a shading language. In VCR a scene renders once per requested time with a transparent clear colour, so 3D layers composite over anything else. Real-time quality in seconds per shot rather than Blender's minutes.
use_when: Product reveals, floating objects and camera orbits that must turn around fast
Over Babylon.js for the larger ecosystem: pmndrs postprocessing, drei, glTF tooling
Over Blender when real-time PBR is enough and the source should stay web-native
Shader-driven visuals through TSL or raw GLSL
avoid_when: Path-traced quality or the compositor: Blender
Step-by-step physics or fluids: Blender caches, or Rapier with fixed-step replay
Mostly 2D with incidental depth: p5.js or PixiJS
React is already the app shell: React Three Fiber on top

facets.one_line: Renderer with alpha, cameras as functions of t, render on the driven frame
glTF and textures loaded before the scene declares itself ready
Standard and physical materials, environment lighting, shadows
Composer passes and which effects are seek-safe
Node materials in JavaScript for the WebGPU renderer
